🇲🇽🚆 <u>Trains and housing are moving nearly 1% of Mexico's GDP</u>

While inspecting the Querétaro–Irapuato line (25% complete, serving 2 million people), Sheinbaum said passenger rail and Vivienda para el Bienestar are the public works doing the most to drive the economy, contributing close to 1% of GDP this year. Mexico is building about 2,500 km of track: roughly 300 km for freight, the rest for intercity and metropolitan passenger service. INEGI's flash estimate put third-quarter growth at 3.2% year on year, the strongest since 2023.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Modalidad 40 now eats 14% of IMSS pension spending</u>

IMSS confirmed that Modalidad 40 — the voluntary-contribution scheme that consulting firms turned into a pension-inflation business — now absorbs 14% of everything the institute pays out in pensions: about 106,680 million pesos out of a bill of roughly 762 billion. At Hacienda's third-quarter public finance briefing, IMSS revenue undersecretary Bertha Gómez Castro warned that this share "is growing." That's the loophole Sheinbaum moved to rein in with the October 22 decree.

🇲🇽🎨 "Remembering is also a way of keeping memory alive." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Palacio Nacional On November 1 she presented the Day of the Dead altar at the National Palace, after joining young people threading cempasúchil for the offering. "Through photographs, anecdotes, aromas and favorite dishes, we remember those who are no longer here and keep alive the bonds that are part of our history. That is how we pass on our traditions from generation to generation." Cempasúchil is native to Mexico. Its Nahuatl name means "20 flowers" or "many flowers." For the Mexica it represented the sun, and by tradition its color and scent guide loved ones back home.

🇲🇽📈 <u>KBRA Keeps Mexico at BBB, Outlook Stable</u>

Kroll Bond Rating Agency ratified Mexico's sovereign rating at BBB with a stable outlook, citing a "solid macroeconomic policy framework," responsible public finances and the economy's resilience to external shocks, El Economista reports. KBRA expects a gradual recovery backed by monetary easing and "growth in real wages." Mexico keeps investment grade with all eight agencies that rate its debt — announced the same day INEGI reported 0.9% quarterly GDP growth in Q3.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Army Recaptures "El Titán," the Gulf Cartel Heir a Judge Let Walk</u>

Army and National Guard troops arrested Axel Alfredo Cárdenas Rodríguez, "El Titán," second-in-command of the Gulf Cartel's Los Ciclones faction and grandnephew of founder Osiel Cárdenas Guillén, in Matamoros on October 29 — at the wheel of a blue Lamborghini Urus. He was flown to Mexico City on an Air Force plane and handed to the organized-crime prosecutors of FEMDO. He had already been arrested in May 2023, but in January 2024 a judge let him continue his case outside the Altiplano prison, and he walked.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Maru Campos to Sheinbaum: "It Wasn't Me, It Was My Ex-Prosecutor"</u>

Sheinbaum revealed what Chihuahua's PAN governor told her at their tense September 19 airport meeting: that former state prosecutor César Jáuregui, now facing trial for treason, was solely responsible for letting four CIA agents into the state without authorization, and that he ran casinos. "When I told her 'agents came in,' she told me: 'it wasn't me, it was my ex-prosecutor,'" the president said. Campos told Attorney General Ernestina Godoy the same. On her claims against Morena's Ariadna Montiel, Sheinbaum's answer: "If you have proof, present it."

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Fuel Smuggling: 61,785 Million Pesos in Dodged Taxes</u>

Cross-checking data from 16 institutions, Mexico's government found 8,824 million liters of fuel in 2025 that didn't add up between what companies bought, moved, invoiced and sold — about 61,785 million pesos in unpaid IEPS tax, Energy Secretary Luz Elena González reported. Trading intermediaries account for 72% of the gaps, gas stations 13%. Sheinbaum now proposes limiting intermediation. The door was opened by Peña Nieto's 2013 energy reform, which handed fuel imports to private players with PRI and PAN votes.

🇲🇽🌧️ <u>Army and Navy Pull 41 People From Los Cabos Floodwaters</u>

Mexico's Defense and Navy ministries activated the DN-III-E and Plan Marina in Baja California Sur and Sonora after Cold Front No. 4 dumped intense rain on the northwest. In Los Cabos, troops rescued 41 people from high-risk areas and recovered 18 vehicles swept away by the currents. In Guaymas, Sonora, two people died when their vehicle was dragged off. Both plans are now in their recovery phase.
